A candidate's tragic death becomes a strategic loophole to control a county board.

California county supervisor candidate dies...
Evidence: Legacy campaign, Strategic appointment, Democratic choice
#Aletheia #USPol

Supporters of deceased candidate Bruce Giudici urge voters to elect him posthumously to honor his legacy and keep his opponent Clyde Clapp off the board.
Stated Judgement: (0.8, 0.4) — Good Preference

The campaign is using a ballot deadline loophole to force a gubernatorial appointment, bypassing a direct democratic choice between active candidates.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.4, 0.6) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — Fall into Deception. The campaign exploits a tragic death to bypass democratic elections in favor of a partisan appointment.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.2, z: 2)

- Giudici Campaign: FAIL (-0.5, 0.7) — Uses tragedy to force a political appointment.
- Clyde Clapp: PASS (0.2, -0.1) — Offered respectful condolences to the family.
Calaveras County supervisor candidate Bruce Giudici died after a fall while campaigning. His campaign continues to run him so the governor can appoint his successor.

The Poison:
By voting for a deceased candidate, citizens surrender their direct democratic franchise to an executive appointment.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is Metaphysical vs Logical. The campaign frames a democratic election as a legacy tribute, while logically engineering a partisan executive appointment.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic pretext loop. The campaign projects a noble desire to honor the dead, but the actual mechanism hoards power by replacing a local democratic vote with a top-down gubernatorial appointment.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. It subverts local democracy under the guise of grief.

The Unavoidable Truth: Bruce Giudici tragically passed away while serving his community.

The Unavoidable Lie: Voting for a deceased candidate is a normal way to express democratic will.

Exploiting a candidate's death to secure a gubernatorial appointment is a cynical subversion of local democracy. Voters deserve a choice among the living.
